title: Lakshya Sen's 13-match winning run ends in Hong Kong Open semi-final
dek: Anders Antonsen beat the Indian in straight games, and Satwik and Chirag also lost, leaving India without a finalist.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Lakshya Sen's 13-match winning run on the badminton World Tour ended in the semi-finals of the Hong Kong Open on Saturday, when Denmark's Anders Antonsen, the third seed and world No. 3, beat him 21-13, 21-13 in 42 minutes at Kai Tak.

Sen had arrived in Hong Kong after winning back-to-back titles at the Hylo Open in Germany and the Kumamoto Masters in Japan. Antonsen controlled both games, and Sen struggled to find his rhythm, according to reports. After the match Sen said his legs had been "pretty tired over the last two weeks", and that fatigue and worries about injury had affected him, according to reports.

India's men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, also went out in the semi-finals, losing 18-21, 19-21 to Malaysia's Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun. It was their second defeat in a row to the Malaysian pair.

The two semi-final defeats end India's campaign at the Super 500 tournament, with no Indian player in Sunday's finals.
